newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Guatemala coffee crop outlook unchanged - Quirin.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala coffee crop outlook unchanged - Quirin.

text.p: Guatemala is still predicting its 1996-1997 coffee crop will come in around 3.5 million 60-kg bags of exportable beans, the president of the National Association of Coffee Growers (Anacafe) said here Wednesday.

Max Quirin, visiting Costa Rica for the country's International Coffee Week, known in Spanish as Sintercafe, said Anacafe had not reviewed its original estimate, which also took into account 300,000 additional bags for domestic consumption.

Quirin, looking further ahead to the future said he thought Guatemala would not signifcantly increase coffee output. "It is difficult to see signs of any significant increase in production in the future," Quirin added.

He said costs were prohibitive and a general shortage of coffee pickers, with Guatemala suffering continuous urban drift awat from the countryside, made investments in expanding plantations not a good business option.

He noted that heavy rains in flowerings, especially in the San Marcos growing region, had delayed the start of the 1996 He noted that heavy rains in flowerings, especially in the San Marcos growing region, had delayed the start of the 1996- 1997 crop but that the situation was returning to normal, although he did predict a few problems for growers fullfilling November shipments with forward sold coffee.

Quirin acknowledged Guatemala exported 200,000 to 300,000 bags of contraband coffee from neighbours Honduras and El Salvador last cycle. "It is no secret to anyone, but I think this year the situation will be normalised because of tax changes in the countries in question," he added, refering to new fiscal regimes in neighbouring nations that have lessened the incentive to export via third party countries.
